suggestions: Replace the short-horizon CLV level with a stock-specific persistence measure: Ma((close-low)/Max((high-low), Med((high-low), 20)), 15) - Med(Ma((close-low)/Max((high-low), Med((high-low), 20)), 15), 60). Rationale: a 5-day average of raw close-location value conflates one-off spikes with genuine behavioral shifts and is highly sensitive to near-zero range days; measuring sustained elevation above each stock's own 60-day norm filters transient noise and reduces sign reversals that drive RankIR instability across years.

Restructure the combination using hierarchical smoothing instead of a raw contemporaneous product: Ma(Ma((close-low)/(high-low), 10) * Ma(Corr(volume, (high-low)/Ma((high-low), 40), 40), 10), 20). Rationale: 20-day rolling correlation on volume and range width is a high-variance estimator whose sign flips frequently in low-participation regimes; smoothing the correlation leg before multiplication and applying an outer 20-day average (mirroring the dual-MA structure of high-RankIR repository alphas) dampens day-to-day coupling noise and yields a more regime-consistent participation-confirmed buying-pressure signal.

Apply cross-sectional ranking to each leg before combining: Rank(Ma((close-low)/Max((high-low), Med((high-low), 20)), 15)) * Rank(Ma(Corr(volume, (high-low)/Ma((high-low), 40), 40), 10)). Rationale: multiplying two heavy-tailed raw series lets outlier stocks dominate portfolio weights and causes distributional shifts across market cycles; rank-normalizing each component before interaction aligns the factor construction with RankIC/RankIR evaluation, compresses tail-driven churn, and improves year-to-year consistency of relative ordering.
